transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-03-17
Time: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: 45 mins
Attendees: Liam (Redwood AE), Sanaa (Redwood SE), Carlos (Redwood SE), Maya (NexaHealth CTO), Ravi (ML Eng), Olivia (Security), Anita (DevOps)

Summary: Weekly POC sync — quick updates on access, env readiness, results from initial hosted runs, and security follow-ups.

[00:00] Liam: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, sorry for the slight delay, um we have the usual folks, Sanaa, Carlos from the SE team, and then Maya, Ravi, Olivia and Anita from NexaHealth, can we do quick round robin?
[00:15] Maya: Yep, Maya here, quick update from our side, Anita's gonna speak to VPC, Ravi will talk about test dataset, Olivia has a couple sec questions on keys.
[00:28] Sanaa: Great, cool. Quick agenda — 1) onboarding/access, 2) initial perf results from the hosted runs, 3) quality issues and tuning, 4) security checklist and next steps. Anything to add?
[00:35] Ravi: No, that sounds right.
[00:40] Anita: We'll want to confirm peering window this week.

[01:02] Liam: Cool. Anita, status on VPC peering and service account?
[01:10] Anita: So we started the peering request yesterday, network asked for the Redwood CIDR and the peering template — we don't have the exact service account yet, so that's blocking automation. I can do a manual rule to unblock tests but we'd prefer peering. Also we need the final network diagram for security to sign off.
[01:30] Sanaa: Right, I can send the network diagram and a CloudFormation snippet today. I'll include the recommended security groups and the minimal IAM role. Expect that by EOD PT.
[01:42] Anita: That helps. Manual rule for now is fine if we need to run a quick bench.

[02:05] Liam: Okay on the bench we ran this morning — quick context: we ran Redwood hosted endpoint with the rdx-1-small-quant variant (note: auto transcribed as red-ex small, transcript glitch) on the clinician prompt set Ravi shared. Average per-token latency was ~180ms, p50 around 120ms, p95 420ms, throughput on sequence length 120 was about 8 reqs/sec. Token cost estimates look in-line with our pilot pricing.
[02:35] Ravi: That's promising. Which model config did you run for kv cache and batching?
[02:42] Carlos: We ran with KV cache enabled and batching at 16 ms window, but quantization at 4-bit for the CPU fallback path. There may be a to-do to tune batch window — right now the p95 spikes when there's a mixed sequence length.
[02:58] Maya: The 180ms avg — is that end-to-end including our network?
[03:03] Sanaa: This was from Redwood hosted endpoint in us-west to our simulated client in the bench; it includes network egress but not your VPC peered path. When we run on dedicated or private with VPC peering we expect lower variance and lower p95.

[03:30] Ravi: We did see a few hallucination cases in the test set — I'll share 3 exact prompts that failed. Some of the responses are hallucinating patient medication dates — which is risky.
[03:44] Sanaa: Can you paste one now?
[03:48] Ravi: Sure, prompt: "Summarize patient note: 03/22/2026 — reports improved sleep after therapy" — model added a medication start date of 01/01/2025, which was not in the note.
[03:58] Carlos: That type of hallucination could be due to unsafe decoding temp or our default prompt template being a bit too free-form. We can tighten system prompts and increase grounding via retrieval or few-shot. Also eval thresholds might be adjusted.

[04:25] Maya: Are you suggesting a retrieval-augmented approach? Our data is sensitive so we want to keep the data in our VPC ideally.
[04:34] Sanaa: Yes retrieval could help and we support on-prem connectors; for the pilot we can simulate retrieval by passing the relevant patient snippet in the prompt. For production, we recommend dedicated with VPC peering or private deployment if data residency/regulatory requires it.

[05:00] Olivia: Quick security Q — audit logs: can we get per-request audit logs and token-level traceability? Also what's the KMS story — do you support customer-managed keys?
[05:10] Liam: Yes, Redwood provides audit logs and request traces in the console; for private deployments we support customer-managed KMS/HSM. For hosted we support CMEK via cloud provider KMS — we can share the exact PKI/KMS diagram.
[05:25] Olivia: And retention? We have a 7-year audit requirement for certain records.
[05:30] Liam: We'll need to check the enterprise add-on for extended retention; I'll include that in the pricing doc.

[05:48] Anita: Back to the environment, we need the exact service account email and the inbound IP ranges if you have any egress static IPs — our security team needs that for peering rules.
[06:00] Sanaa: We'll provide recommended egress ranges; for hosted there's dynamic ranges but we can provide a list used by our region or suggest dedicated so you get static egress.

[06:20] Ravi: On the quality side — are you doing any supervised finetune or instruction-tuning for the clinician domain or just prompt engineering?
[06:29] Carlos: For the pilot we do prompt engineering and small instruction tuning in-house — we can run a finetune if you provide labeled examples; often retrieval + prompt engineering gives the best FTE-to-quality ROI. We can run a small calibration job as a follow-up.

[06:55] Maya: Performance: what about cost trade-offs — if we move to dedicated or private and enable quantization and batching, what's the expected latency delta?
[07:05] Sanaa: Dedicated with pinned GPU capacity and optimized kernels typically reduces mean latency by 20-40% and dramatically reduces p95 variance. Quantization reduces GPU memory and can increase throughput but sometimes adds 10-30ms overhead per token depending on kernel. We'll produce a short doc with expected ranges for your workload.

[07:37] Olivia: Compliance: Do you have SOC2 and ISO certs? And do you support SAML SSO?
[07:44] Liam: Yes, SOC2 Type II in 2026, ISO 27001 in 2025. We support SAML/SSO and SCIM for user provisioning. I'll push the security pack after this call.

[08:05] Maya: Great. Any blockers to run the dedicated bench next week?
[08:11] Sanaa: Main blockers — peering confirmation and service account; sample failing prompts from Ravi to reproduce hallucinations; and Olivia's KMS requirements. If those are addressed we can spin up a dedicated bench with KV caching and quantization toggles.

[08:30] Ravi: I'll drop the three failing prompts and the test dataset link in the CRM ticket by EOD tomorrow.
[08:36] Olivia: I'll confirm KMS/HSM requirements and send policy snippets.

[08:50] Liam: Cool — recap of next steps: Sanaa to send network diagram and CFN; Liam to send pricing and security pack; Ravi to share failing prompts and dataset; Olivia to confirm KMS needs; Anita to confirm peering window. We'll schedule the deep dive bench for w/c 2027-03-29.

[09:12] Maya: Sounds good. Anything else?
[09:16] Carlos: We'll also include a minimal reproducible bench script so you can run locally against the hosted endpoint if needed.

[09:30] Liam: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in CRM and cc docs. End call.

Notes: Transcript contains minor auto-transcription errors (model name rendered as red-ex etc.). References to docs: "SOC2 pack", "network diagram", "bench script". Links will be shared in follow-up email.
